doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Discrimination on the road with Carter
summary: Less discrimination than with the earlier bands in smaller towns.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you find that there were problems with discrimination in traveling with that band, just as there had been earlier with the other bands that you had been with?
Much less. Minimal. It was there, yes, but minimal.
I was wondering since you went to larger cities and more supposedly cosmopolitan areas, if you encountered the same problems that you did in the smaller towns on the other kinds of circuits.
Much less of it. It was there, but not as prevalent. We didn’t come into contact with it as much.
